findings.explanation: Multiple agents independently state they are doing the same merge task without a clear verification or handoff: [M2] says “doing the whole thing myself; no need to duplicate,” and [M3] says “I’m writing the merge script and outputs; no need to duplicate.” Both are materially equivalent execution of the assigned task rather than a deliberate independent check or synthesis. [M4], [M5], and [M7] then report overlapping completion of the same outputs, reinforcing the duplicate execution pattern.

The task was acknowledged and later delivered: [M2] and [M3] both explicitly acknowledge the work, [M4] and [M5] report outputs written, and [M7] also confirms completion. There is no clear abandonment, missing acknowledgement, or unresolved ownership gap in the visible messages.

The later messages do not show any relevant visible information being ignored or contradicted without resolution. The completion messages consistently align on the same outputs and counts ([M4], [M5], [M7]), so there is no clear missed opportunity to use prior information in a decision.

annotations.rationale: The message assigns a concrete multi-step data integration task with explicit input/output requirements and conflict handling rules. It requests work to be done rather than providing results or asking a question.

evidence.text: Merge user data from three different sources with different formats and schemas.
Handle conflicts using source priority (source_a > source_b > source_c)
